CAT.rationale: CAT is a high-quality franchise with durable competitive advantages (dominant dealer network, 16%+ market share, $51.2B backlog, structural AI/data center power tailwind). However, the stock has undergone a ~3x P/E expansion over 12 months (13.7x to 40.1x) with ZERO fundamental improvement to justify it — ROE flat at 55%, net margin flat at ~15.7%, and EPS actually declining 3.6% YoY in Q3 2025. The earnings yield of 2.5% is now below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.34%, implying a negative equity risk premium for a cyclical industrial — an historically unsustainable condition. Simultaneously, margins are compressing (~370bp gross margin contraction YoY), $2.6B in tariff costs loom for 2026, Cat Financial profit plunged 61% in Q4 2025, and a CFO transition adds execution uncertainty. The Q1 2026 earnings report (April 30) is a near-term catalyst, but at 40x trailing earnings with declining EPS, even a beat is unlikely to justify the multiple. A reversion to 20x P/E (mid-range) implies ~50% downside. The risk/reward is extremely unfavorable.
